newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Govt support for banks gets harder to gauge - Moodys.
newsitem.headline: Govt support for banks gets harder to gauge - Moodys.

text.p: Predicting the circumstances in which government authorities will support troubled banks is becoming increasingly complex, Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday.
The traditional view that support is determined by whether a bank is "too big to fail" is becoming less adequate, the rating agency said in a report.

"The concept of "too big to fail" remains valid, but its relative importance within the constellation of issues which determine the likelihood of support has diminished as other issues have come to the fore," the report said.

Recent bank failures around the world indicate that the domestic financial policy and the circumstances leading up to a bank's failure are just as important as the bank's size in determining the willingness of financial authorities to prevent a default, Moody's said.
